correctness.rationale: With \(G_r=\mathbb F_3^r\), the group-algebra augmentation ideal has nilpotence index \(2r+1\); the identity coefficient of the zero-subset product yields the exact Davenport bound. The six displayed rank-three terms admit no zero-sum index subset (third-coordinate case split), meet different lines, and hence each complementary image of length five forces a nonzero return in the quotient by its line. Adding two terms with fresh final coordinate one preserves both properties for every greater rank. For ranks one and two the case split on four possible terms proves existence of a separating line; all 184 rank-two zero-sum-free unordered multisequences were also enumerated independently.
